alignments.note: Construct noun with the supplied indefinite article, which belongs to the nominal expression under rule 15 and is not `added`.
Article on the rectum; the ASV writes no *the* for the chain (*A Song of Ascents*), so the morpheme is unrepresented under rule 29.
Nomen rectum takes the chain's relational *of* under rule 19, headed on the noun.
Preposition rendered *of* before the name.
Proper name.
Vocative divine name; the ASV writes no supplied *O* here, so the noun takes only its own word (rule 36).
Negative particle taking the written *not*; discontinuous from the predicate under rule 25.
Finite verb recast with a copula and predicate adjective; both words belong to the verb's unit under rule 17, headed on the lexical predicate *haughty* under rule 24.
Construct noun keeps its own word.
Pronominal suffix realized by the possessive *my* (rule 18).
Waw plus negative fused into the single *nor* under rule 35, headed on the negative, which is what distinguishes it from a bare *and*.
Finite verb rendered by the predicate adjective *lofty*; the copula is gapped from the preceding colon and the ASV writes none here, so only the one word is placed.
Construct noun.
Suffix realized by the possessive *mine* (rule 18).
Waw plus negative fused into *Neither* under rule 35, headed on the negative.

Finite verb with its fronted auxiliary, subject pronoun and lexical verb under rule 17; the reflexive *myself* renders the Piel's own sense and stays with the verb under rule 44 rather than being marked `added`. Headed on the lexical verb.
Preposition rendered *in*.

Anarthrous substantival adjective with the generic noun the ASV supplies to make it an English noun phrase (rule 46); headed on *great*, the word carrying the lexeme, by rule 31's subtraction test — *matters* alone is any matters.
Waw rendered by the connective *Or* under rule 14.
Preposition rendered *in*.
Niphal participle used substantivally with the supplied generic *things* (rule 46), headed on *wonderful*; the unit is discontinuous around the *too* that belongs to the comparative preposition.

Comparative `מִן` rendered by the *too … for* frame; rule 24 gives both words to that one morpheme's discontinuous unit and heads it on the relational word *for*, since dropping *for* leaves the comparison with no relation stated. The competing reading leaves *too* with the participle, but rule 11 gives the function word first to the morpheme whose sense it carries.
Suffix realized by the object pronoun *me* (rule 18).

review_notes: The ASV's marginal gloss *Hebrew walk* on *exercise myself* was read and set aside under rule 38; the printed text governs.
Both `וְ` + `לֹא` pairs are fused under rule 35 and headed on the negative; the two colons are read alike.
